belief_statement: Preliminary evidence indicates that ability design effectiveness screening has inconsistent effects on noise. The evidence base (3 findings, 1 studies) is growing but not yet conclusive.

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Distraction Theory, Psychophysics / Perception). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of ability design effectiveness screening, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: Does the effect of ability design effectiveness screening on noise replicate in a pre-registered RCT?
research_needs.rationale: Current confidence is moderate. A well-powered pre-registered replication would most efficiently resolve the status of this belief.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains ability design effectiveness screening → noise?
research_needs.rationale: 2 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for ability design effectiveness screening effects on noise?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.
